headline: Reference genome assemblies for pest, vector and model arthropods
label: Chromosome Level Genome Assemblies
summary: Recent reports release new reference genomes for an invasive gall wasp, four West Nile virus Culex vectors and a soil ecotoxicology model mite.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the generation of reference genomes for arthropods of applied relevance, spanning a pest, disease vectors and a toxicology model. The Quadrastichus erythrinae preprint reports a chromosome-level 399 Mb assembly of an invasive wiliwili pest gall wasp and also yields the genome of its Wolbachia endosymbiont. The ERGA-BGE report presents chromosome-level reference genomes for four Mediterranean Culex species that are key West Nile virus vectors, with contig and scaffold metrics. The Oppia nitens paper is a different class of resource: a hybrid de novo draft of 125.4 Mb in 65 scaffolds, with N50 of 4.41 Mb and 99.1% BUSCO completeness, for a soil ecotoxicology model. What is new is a multi-species comparative set of vector genomes within one genus and an endosymbiont genome reported alongside its host. These works report assembly quality and structure only and do not address the biological mechanisms of vector competence or toxicant response.
